import { bookingResponsesDbSchema } from "@calcom/features/bookings/lib/getBookingResponsesSchema";
import slugify from "@calcom/lib/slugify";
import type { PrismaClient } from "@calcom/prisma";
import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";
import type { Prisma } from "@calcom/prisma/client";
import { MembershipRole } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";

type BookingSelect = {
  description: true;
  customInputs: true;
  attendees: {
    select: {
      email: true;
      name: true;
    };
  };
  location: true;
};

// Backward Compatibility for booking created before we had managed booking questions
function getResponsesFromOldBooking(
  rawBooking: Prisma.BookingGetPayload<{
    select: BookingSelect;
  }>
) {
  const customInputs = rawBooking.customInputs || {};
  const responses = Object.keys(customInputs).reduce((acc, label) => {
    acc[slugify(label) as keyof typeof acc] = customInputs[label as keyof typeof customInputs];
    return acc;
  }, {});
  return {
    // It is possible to have no attendees in a booking when the booking is cancelled.
    name: rawBooking.attendees[0]?.name || "Nameless",
    email: rawBooking.attendees[0]?.email || "",
    guests: rawBooking.attendees.slice(1).map((attendee) => {
      return attendee.email;
    }),
    notes: rawBooking.description || "",
    location: {
      value: rawBooking.location || "",
      optionValue: rawBooking.location || "",
    },
    ...responses,
  };
}

async function getBooking(prisma: PrismaClient, uid: string, isSeatedEvent?: boolean) {
  const rawBooking = await prisma.booking.findUnique({
    where: {
      uid,
    },
    select: {
      id: true,
      uid: true,
      startTime: true,
      endTime: true,
      description: true,
      customInputs: true,
      responses: true,
      smsReminderNumber: true,
      location: true,
      eventTypeId: true,
      status: true,
      userId: true,
      eventType: {
        select: {
          disableRescheduling: true,
          minimumRescheduleNotice: true,
        },
      },
....
    responses: isSeatedEvent ? booking.responses : booking.responses || getResponsesFromOldBooking(booking),
  } as Omit<T, "responses"> & { responses: Record<string, any> };
};

export default getBooking;

export const getBookingForReschedule = async (uid: string, userId?: number) => {
  let rescheduleUid: string | null = null;
  const theBooking = await prisma.booking.findUnique({
    where: {
      uid,
    },
    select: {
      id: true,
      userId: true,
      user: {
        select: {
          organizationId: true,
        },
      },
      eventType: {
        select: {
          seatsPerTimeSlot: true,
          teamId: true,
          hosts: {
            select: {
              userId: true,
            },
          },
          owner: {
            select: {
              id: true,
            },
          },
        },
      },
    },
  });
  let bookingSeatReferenceUid: number | null = null;

  // If no booking is found via the uid, it's probably a booking seat
  // that its being rescheduled, which we query next.
  let attendeeEmail: string | null = null;
  let bookingSeatData: {
    description?: string;
    responses: Prisma.JsonValue;
  } | null = null;
  if (!theBooking) {
    const bookingSeat = await prisma.bookingSeat.findFirst({
      where: {
        referenceUid: uid,
      },
      select: {
        id: true,
        attendee: {
          select: {
            name: true,
            email: true,
          },
        },
        data: true,
        booking: {
          select: {
            uid: true,
          },
        },
      },
    });
    if (bookingSeat) {
      bookingSeatData = bookingSeat.data as unknown as {
        description?: string;
        responses: Prisma.JsonValue;
      };
      bookingSeatReferenceUid = bookingSeat.id;
      rescheduleUid = bookingSeat.booking.uid;
      attendeeEmail = bookingSeat.attendee.email;
    }
  }

  // If we have the booking and not bookingSeat, we need to make sure the booking belongs to the userLoggedIn
  // Otherwise, we return null here.
  let hasOwnershipOnBooking = false;
  if (theBooking?.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot && bookingSeatReferenceUid === null) {
    const isOwnerOfBooking = theBooking.userId === userId;

    const isHostOfEventType = theBooking?.eventType?.hosts.some((host) => host.userId === userId);

    const isUserIdInBooking = theBooking.userId === userId;

    if (!isOwnerOfBooking && !isHostOfEventType && !isUserIdInBooking) return null;
    hasOwnershipOnBooking = true;
  }

  // If we don't have a booking and no rescheduleUid, the ID is invalid,
  // and we return null here.
  if (!theBooking && !rescheduleUid) return null;

  const booking = await getBooking(prisma, rescheduleUid || uid, !!bookingSeatReferenceUid);

  if (!booking) return null;

  if (bookingSeatReferenceUid) {
    booking.description = bookingSeatData?.description ?? null;
    booking.responses = bookingResponsesDbSchema.parse(bookingSeatData?.responses ?? {});
  }
  return {
    ...booking,
    attendees: rescheduleUid
      ? booking.attendees.filter((attendee) => attendee.email === attendeeEmail)
      : hasOwnershipOnBooking
        ? []
        : booking.attendees,
  };
};

  return (

        />

            .

        <div className="flex justify-end mt-auto space-x-2 modalsticky rtl:space-x-reverse">
          {!!onCancel && (
            <Button

              className={classNames?.backButton}>
              {t("back")}

);

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 21:48:57Z)**_

The whole series reschedule is built and every automated check passes, but I haven't clicked through it in a browser yet, and nothing is committed.

**Checks:**
- **Type check:** `yarn type-check:ci --force` passes (9 of 9 tasks).
- **Tests:** all pass. That includes 4 new series-reschedule tests, 6 for the conflict helper and 7 date-calculation tests including both daylight-saving changes. I also ran the whole booking handler and service folder (167 tests) to catch regressions in ordinary bookings.
- **The self-exclusion test catches the bug it should:** when I temporarily removed the per-date uid swap, 3 of the new tests failed, then I restored it.
- **Lint:** Biome reports nothing on the new files.

**How it works:**
- **Choosing the scope:** the reschedule form shows "This occurrence / This and all following" when more than one occurrence remains ([BookEventForm.tsx](apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookEventForm/BookEventForm.tsx)).
- **New times:** each remaining occurrence moves by the same number of calendar days and gets the new clock time in the attendee's timezone ([shift-recurring-series.ts](packages/lib/shift-recurring-series.ts)).
- **Conflict check:** before anything is written, every date is checked against availability and the booking window. Each date ignores its own old booking ([RegularBookingService.ts](packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts), [getSeriesRescheduleConflicts.ts](packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/getSeriesRescheduleConflicts.ts)).
- **If any date conflicts:** the user sees every conflicting date in their timezone, and nothing changes.
- **Otherwise:** each old booking is rescheduled one-for-one through the existing flow. The series keeps its ID, and one email goes out.
- **Entry points:** the Reschedule link now appears for recurring bookings on the booking page and in emails.

**Where I changed the plan:**
- **Guard location:** the check that every uid is unique and belongs to this series lives in `RegularBookingService`, not `RecurringBookingService`. That avoids changing a DI module.
- **Extra status check:** the guard also rejects occurrences that are no longer ACCEPTED or PENDING. Otherwise, an occurrence cancelled after the page loaded would make the reschedule fail partway through.
- **Type fix:** adding `seriesOccurrences` to `GetBookingType` accidentally removed its `| null`, which broke three web files. I fixed the type itself.
- **Extra file:** the Booker test utility needed the new store field.
- **Formatting reverted:** `biome check --write` had also sorted imports and reformatted lines I didn't touch. The pre-commit hook only lints, so I reverted that churn to keep the diff about the feature.

**Size: larger than I estimated.** It's about 720 changed lines across 18 code files: roughly 350 of production code and 370 of tests. I estimated 450–500, so the PR description should say so.

**Known gaps to mention in the PR:**
- **Not atomic:** the writes happen one booking at a time. A failure after the pre-check passes, such as a slot taken in a race, would leave some occurrences moved and others not.
- **Approval emails:** when an event requires confirmation, the host's approval sends one email per date.
- **False conflicts on large shifts:** the series' other old bookings still count as busy, so moving it by a full week or more can report a conflict that isn't real. In that case nothing changes.
- **Not changed:** the reschedule text in platform customers' calendar descriptions, and the host no-show screen. Both are outside this issue.

**Not done yet:**
- The manual check from the plan: book a series, reschedule it, block a date, and try it with confirmation required.
- Committing and opening the draft PR. Two existing changes aren't mine and should stay out of the commit: `.vscode/settings.json` and `agents/cal-diy-spec-sheet.html`.

Should I commit and open the draft PR, or would you rather do the manual check first?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 21:53:25Z)**_

I added the guard test, and the code side of the plan is now complete.

**Why it was missing:** I wrote the duplicate-uid test and counted it as covering the guard, and I didn't check my tests against the plan's list before telling you the work was done. The guard has two separate checks:
- **Uniqueness:** the duplicate-uid test covered this.
- **Membership:** that every uid belongs to this series. This is what stops a request from moving bookings in a different series, and it had no test.

**The new test:**
- **Setup:** it seeds one extra booking that belongs to a different series, then sends a reschedule request for occurrence 1, that other booking, and occurrence 3.
- **What it checks:** the request is rejected with `BadRequest`, this series is unchanged, and the other series' booking is still ACCEPTED at its original time.
- **Where:** a `withOtherSeriesBooking` option on the existing `setupSeries` helper in [RecurringBookingService.test.ts](packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RecurringBookingService.test.ts). It's off by default, so the other tests run exactly as before.

**Results:**
- All 6 series tests pass.
- With the membership check temporarily removed, only the new test failed, so it tests that check specifically. I've restored the check.

Still open from the plan: the manual browser check and the commits/draft PR. Round-robin and team events still have no test of their own.

## Grades for the current changes

| Criterion | Score | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Correctness** | **8/10** | Meets all three acceptance criteria: the scope choice, every date checked with the conflicting dates listed and nothing changed, and one email. I checked two risks just now and both are fine: calendar updates ignore the series rule, and skipping `onBookingRescheduled` matches series creation. Deductions: writes after the pre-check aren't atomic; a shift of a week or more can report false conflicts; and none of it has been checked in a browser yet. |
| **Test coverage** | **7/10** | The backend and the pure helpers are well covered, including DST and the guard, and I confirmed the self-exclusion and membership tests fail when their checks are removed. Gaps: (a) the success test only counts emails (`length === 2`), so it never checks that they're *rescheduled* emails; (b) `mapSeriesRescheduleToMutationInput` has no test; (c) the guard can only be tested through the slow integration setup; (d) no tests for round-robin, team events, requires-confirmation, or the UI. |
| **Code quality** | **7/10** | Follows the existing patterns (repository, ErrorWithCode, store, no `as any`), and the names are clear. Issues: (a) about 65 lines of series logic sit inline in a 2,700-line handler, including a guard rule that can't be tested on its own; (b) the "ACCEPTED or PENDING" rule is **duplicated** in `RegularBookingService` and `get-booking.ts`; (c) `RecurringBookingService` redeclares the date type inline instead of reusing `SeriesRescheduleDate`. |
| **Documentation** | **5/10** | The inline comments explain *why*, as the repo rules require. But the **PR description doesn't exist yet**, so half of this criterion is missing. |

## Fixes, in order

1. Move the guard and the status rule into the helper file. This removes the duplication, shrinks the handler, and makes the guard unit-testable.
2. Reuse `SeriesRescheduleDate` in `RecurringBookingService`.
3. Make the success test check that the emails are actually rescheduled emails.
4. Add a unit test for the mapper.
5. Draft the PR description.

I'm not changing the non-atomic writes or the false conflicts on large shifts. Fixing either would mean the large rewrites we already decided against, so they belong in the PR description as known limitations instead.

### Fix 1: move the guard and status rule into [getSeriesRescheduleConflicts.ts](packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/getSeriesRescheduleConflicts.ts)

- **What:** add two exported functions to the helper file:
  - `isReschedulableOccurrenceStatus(status)`: the single definition of "ACCEPTED or PENDING".
  - `hasInvalidSeriesRescheduleUids(requestedUids, occurrences)`: the guard (unique uids, each one a reschedulable occurrence of this series).
- **Why:** the "reschedulable" status rule currently lives in two places, `RegularBookingService` and `get-booking.ts`. If someone updates one and not the other, the form could offer an occurrence the server then rejects. A pure function can also be unit-tested without the booking-scenario setup.
- **How it fits:** this keeps all series-reschedule rules in one file next to the conflict helper. It imports `BookingStatus` from `@calcom/prisma/enums` as a type-free value import, the same way `RegularBookingService` already does.

25	export async function getSeriesRescheduleConflicts(
26	  dates: SeriesRescheduleDate[],
27	  checkDate: (date: SeriesRescheduleDate) => Promise<unknown>
28	): Promise<string[]> {
29	  const results = await Promise.allSettled(dates.map((date) => checkDate(date)));
30	
31	  const conflictingDates: string[] = [];
32	  results.forEach((result, index) => {
33	    if (result.status === "fulfilled") return;
34	    if (!isDateUnavailableError(result.reason)) throw result.reason;
35	    conflictingDates.push(dates[index].start);
36	  });
37	
38	  return conflictingDates;
39	}

42	 * Availability checks only read the rescheduled booking's uid (to skip it as busy) and its duration.
43	 * Every occurrence in a series has the same duration, so swapping the uid lets each new date skip
44	 * the old occurrence it replaces instead of only the first one.
45	 */
46	export function withRescheduleUidForDate<T extends { uid: string }>(
47	  booking: T | null,
48	  date: { rescheduleUid?: string }
49	): T | null {
50	  if (!booking || !date.rescheduleUid) return booking;
51	  return { ...booking, uid: date.rescheduleUid };
52	}

## Final grades

| Criterion | Before | After | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Correctness** | 8 | **8** | Meets all three acceptance criteria. I checked two possible problems and both are fine: moving a calendar event doesn't turn it into a new series, and the skipped `onBookingRescheduled` step only counts private-link uses. Still capped at 8 by three things the fixes didn't change: the writes aren't atomic, a shift of a week or more can report false conflicts, and nothing has been checked in a browser. |
| **Test coverage** | 7 | **8.5** | Added unit tests for the guard (all five ways a request can be rejected), for the status rule, and for the mapper. The success test now checks that both emails are *rescheduled* emails, not just that two were sent. Pointing that check at the wrong email title makes it fail, so it's a real check. Still untested: round-robin and team events, requires-confirmation, and the form UI. |
| **Code quality** | 7 | **8.5** | The "ACCEPTED or PENDING" rule now lives in one function that both the reschedule page and the server guard use. The guard moved out of the 2,700-line handler into a small tested function. `RecurringBookingService` reuses the `SeriesRescheduleDate` type. The remaining weakness is that the series pre-check still sits inline in a very large handler, which is how the rest of that handler is written. |
| **Documentation** | 5 | **5** | The inline comments explain *why*, as the repo rules require. There's no PR description because you asked me not to draft one, and this criterion grades it. |

## What changed

1. **Guard and status rule:** moved into [getSeriesRescheduleConflicts.ts](packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/getSeriesRescheduleConflicts.ts), and used from both `RegularBookingService` and `get-booking.ts`.
2. **Shared type:** `RecurringBookingService` uses `SeriesRescheduleDate` instead of its own copy.
3. **Tests:** 7 new guard and status unit tests, and the success test now checks the email titles.
4. **Mapper tests:** new [booking-to-mutation-input-mapper.test.ts](packages/features/bookings/lib/client/booking-event-form/booking-to-mutation-input-mapper.test.ts) with 3 tests.

Yes, it could be condensed. I merged my series branch with the existing recurring-date check right below it, since the two duplicated the same per-date availability logic.

**Result:**
- **Handler growth:** the PR now adds 24 lines to `RegularBookingService` instead of 75. The diff is +67/−43 because it replaces the old loop rather than adding a second copy beside it.
- **One per-date check:** `checkDateIsAvailable` is the only place that decides which hosts must be free on a date. It works for both new series and series reschedules.
- **Shorter calls:** the `?? undefined` workaround is gone from both call sites, after the type check confirmed the field accepts `null`.

**How the merged block reads now:**
1. Take the first `numSlotsToCheckForAvailability` dates: all of them for a series reschedule, only the first for a new series.
2. **Series reschedule:** run the guard, then check every date in parallel (booking window plus `checkDateIsAvailable`), and report all conflicts.
3. **New series:** run `checkDateIsAvailable` on each date in order and stop at the first error, as before.

**Checks:**
- **Type check:** passes (9 of 9).
- **Tests:** all 260 across 33 files pass, including the 167 existing booking-handler and service tests. Those cover ordinary and recurring bookings that don't go through the new path, so behaviour there is unchanged.
- **Lint:** Biome reports nothing in the refactored lines.

**What I left alone:** the round-robin host loop further down has its own per-date check. Merging it into `checkDateIsAvailable` would mean rewriting how the existing round-robin code picks a host, which is a riskier change and outside this issue. It already shares the per-date exclusion through `withRescheduleUidForDate`.

With this, I'd move code quality from 8.5 to about **9/10**. The remaining limit is that the block still lives inside a very large handler.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 22:12:35Z)**_

Only the browser check needs to happen for this issue. The other two don't affect the acceptance criteria, and fixing them would be much bigger than the issue itself.

**1. Non-atomic writes: no, not for this issue.**
- **What the issue asks:** "If any date has a conflict, the system says which dates and makes no changes." That's met. Every conflict, booking-window problem, or bad uid is caught before anything is written, and the tests confirm nothing changes.
- **Where it can still go wrong:** a failure after that check, such as someone booking the slot in the moment between the check and the writes, or a database error partway through. The issue doesn't ask for protection against that.
- **Existing behaviour:** creating a new recurring series has the same limitation today.
- **Cost of fixing it:** one transaction across many bookings, plus undoing calendar changes. We ruled that out in design decision #6.
- **What to do:** mention it as a known limitation in the PR.

**2. False conflicts on large shifts: no, but it's narrower than "a week or more" suggests.**
- **When it actually happens:** only when a new date lands on top of a *different* old occurrence. That means moving the series by whole weeks to an overlapping time, for example Tue 2pm → the following Tue 2pm, which is really postponing the series rather than changing its time.
- **The issue's scenario is fine:** Tue 2pm → Thu 3pm, or any move to a different day or time, never hits it.
- **When it does happen, it fails safe:** the user sees "these dates conflict" and nothing changes.
- **Cost of fixing it:** the availability code that every booking depends on would need to exclude a whole list of bookings instead of one, which touches about 6–8 core files. We weighed that in #5 and rejected it.
- **What to do:** mention it as a known limitation in the PR.

**3. Browser check: yes, before the PR is marked ready.**
This isn't about the code being wrong. It's that a lot of what the user actually sees has no automated test:
- the "This occurrence / This and all following" radio (acceptance criterion 1)
- the Reschedule link on the booking page and in emails
- the conflict message with dates formatted in the attendee's timezone
- the redirect to the success page after a series reschedule
- the requires-confirmation path

The plan's manual steps 1–4 cover all of these. Running the app needs a local database and `yarn dev`, and the repo's rules say to ask before full builds. You can run it yourself, or I can try with the `run` skill. Which would you prefer?

Here's a manual test plan covering everything the automated tests don't: the reschedule page UI, the links, the emails, and the confirmation flow. Plan on about 30–45 minutes.

## Setup (once)

1. **Database:** `yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-setup`. This starts Postgres in Docker, runs migrations and seeds the test users. Host login: `pro` / `pro`.
2. **Email catcher:** the repo's `.env` sends email to `localhost:1025`, but `docker-compose.yml` has no mail catcher. Run one:
   `docker run -d -p 1025:1025 -p 8025:8025 axllent/mailpit`, then open http://localhost:8025 to see emails.
3. **App:** `yarn dev`, then open http://localhost:3000 and log in as `pro`.
4. **Event type:** create "Weekly session", 30 min. On its **Recurring** tab, turn on "Recurring event", repeat every **1 week**, up to **4** occurrences. Keep the default working hours.

Book as the attendee in a **private/incognito window**, so you're not logged in as the host.

## Test 1: Reschedule the whole series (criteria 1 and 3)

1. In incognito, open `localhost:3000/pro/weekly-session`. Pick a **Tuesday 2pm** next week, keep 4 occurrences, and book with a test email.
2. Clear the Mailpit inbox.
3. On the booking success page, check that a **Reschedule** link now appears. It used to be hidden for recurring bookings.
4. Click it and pick **Thursday 3pm** in the same week.
5. **Expect:** above the button, "This occurrence" and "This and all following (4 occurrences)". Choose the second, then click Reschedule.

**Expected results:**
- You land on the success page.
- Mailpit has **exactly 2 emails**, one to the attendee and one to the host. Both are "rescheduled" emails and say it repeats weekly for 4 occurrences.
- As the host, **Bookings → Upcoming** shows 4 Thursdays at **3pm**. The Tuesdays are gone from Upcoming and show up under Cancelled/Past as rescheduled.
- Optional database check: `yarn db-studio`, then look at the Booking table filtered by that `recurringEventId`. Expect 4 new ACCEPTED rows, each with `fromReschedule` set, and 4 old rows CANCELLED with `rescheduled = true`.

## Test 2: "This occurrence" still moves only one

Reschedule one occurrence and choose **This occurrence**. Only that one booking moves, and the others stay on Thursday.

## Test 3: Conflict on a later date (criterion 2)

1. As the host: **Availability → your schedule → Date overrides**. Mark the **Friday of week 3** of the series as unavailable.
2. As the attendee, reschedule the series, choose **This and all following**, and pick **Friday 10am in week 1**.

**Expected results:**
- An error says the new time isn't available on that Friday (week 3), with the date shown in the attendee's timezone, and says nothing was changed.
- Bookings → Upcoming is unchanged, and no new emails arrive.

Remove the date override afterwards.

## Test 4: Booking window

1. With the series in place, open the event type's **Limits** tab and set "Limit future bookings" to **14 days**.
2. Reschedule the series ("This and all following").

**Expected:** an error listing the dates beyond 14 days, and nothing changes. Turn the limit off afterwards.

## Test 5: Host must re-approve (the issue's open question)

1. On the event type's **Advanced** tab, turn on **Requires confirmation**.
2. Book a new series as the attendee, then approve it as the host under **Bookings → Unconfirmed**.
3. Reschedule that series as the attendee ("This and all following").

**Expected results:**
- All the new bookings show as **Unconfirmed**.
- Mailpit gets **one** request email to the host and one to the attendee.
- The host approves once (Unconfirmed/Recurring tab) and every date becomes accepted.
- Known side effect: approving sends one confirmation email **per date**.

## Test 6: Reschedule link in the email

Open the attendee's confirmation email in Mailpit. "Need to make a change?" should now show **Reschedule** as well as Cancel for the recurring booking, and clicking it should open the reschedule page.

## Test 7: Edge cases

- **Last occurrence:** reschedule only the **last** occurrence. No radio should appear, because only one occurrence remains.
- **Timezone (optional):** change the timezone dropdown on the booking page to a different timezone, repeat Test 3, and check that the conflict date is shown in that timezone.

## Not testable locally

Moving events in Google Calendar needs a connected Google account with credentials. Without one, calendar updates are skipped. The automated tests cover that part with a mock calendar.

If anything fails, send me the step and what you saw, plus the server log from `yarn dev`, and I'll trace it.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 22:16:47Z)**_

The cause is almost certainly that **Docker isn't running**, not the feature code. Both the login page and `/pro` return 500. Those pages don't use anything from this change, and both need the database, which isn't reachable:
- your `.env` points the database at `localhost:5450`, the Postgres container that `db-setup` creates
- the Docker daemon isn't running ("Cannot connect to the Docker daemon"), so that container isn't running
- nothing is listening on port 5450

**To fix it:**
1. **Start Docker Desktop:** open it from Applications, or run `open -a Docker`. Wait until it says it's running.
2. **Start the database:**
   - If you've never run setup: `yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-setup`. That starts Postgres, runs migrations and seeds the `pro`/`free` users.
   - If you have, just start the container: `yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-up`.
3. **Start the email catcher:** `docker run -d -p 1025:1025 -p 8025:8025 axllent/mailpit`, then open http://localhost:8025.
4. **Reload** http://localhost:3000. If you still get 500s, stop `yarn dev` and start it again so it reconnects to the database.

If the login page loads but you still get a 500 somewhere in the test steps, for example when opening the reschedule page or submitting, that one could be from the new code. Send me the error from the `yarn dev` terminal and which step it happened on, and I'll trace it. I can also start Docker and the database myself if you'd like.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 22:19:29Z)**_

No. "Occurrences" means **how many times the meeting happens in total**, not days of the week. A weekly series with 4 occurrences is one meeting a week for 4 weeks:

> Tue Sep 1 · Tue Sep 8 · Tue Sep 15 · Tue Sep 22

On the event type's **Recurring** tab, after you turn on **Recurring event**, the settings read:

> **Repeats every** `1` `week` **For a maximum of** `4` **events**

- Set the first box to **1** and the unit to **week**.
- Set "For a maximum of" to **4**.

The meeting's day comes from the slot the attendee picks when booking. Pick a Tuesday and all 4 meetings fall on Tuesdays. When booking, the attendee can also choose fewer occurrences, up to that maximum of 4.

Four is just a convenient size for testing: enough that "This and all following" moves several meetings, and a conflict on week 3 (Test 3) or the 14-day limit (Test 4) affects some dates but not all.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 22:21:13Z)**_

Creating the event type as `pro` in your normal window was the right first step. Next you book it as a customer would.

**Why a private window:** the host (`pro`) and the attendee need to be different people. A private window isn't logged in, so you can act as the attendee there while staying logged in as `pro` in your normal window.

**Steps:**
1. **Get the booking link.** In your normal window, on the **Event Types** page, find "Weekly session" and copy its link, using the copy-link button or the link shown under the title. It will look like `http://localhost:3000/pro/weekly-session`.
2. **Open a private window:** in Chrome, ⌘ + Shift + N.
3. **Paste the link** there. You'll see the public booking page for "Weekly session".
4. **Book a series:**
   - Pick a **Tuesday next week**, then the **2:00pm** slot.
   - Leave it at **4** occurrences.
   - Enter any name and a made-up email, such as `student@example.com`, and confirm.
5. **Check the success page.** You should see a confirmation listing the 4 dates. At the bottom, "Need to make a change?" should now offer **Reschedule**.

Then go back to **Test 1** in my earlier message, from step 3 onwards. You'll click **Reschedule**, pick **Thursday 3pm**, choose **"This and all following"**, and check the results.

If you don't see 2:00pm on Tuesday, pick any time that is offered. The test works with any day and time; only the expected results would show different times.
